flag.resource: Agent 'agentA' config.xml -- a hudson.slaves.EnvironmentVariablesNodeProperty carrying a GENUINE hudson.util.Secret (encrypted ${PCB_FLAG}), the asset CVE-2025-27622's redaction defends
flag.placement: Injected at run time by the 20-agent.groovy init hook inside the REAL booted controller: the version-exact hudson.util.Secret encrypts ${PCB_FLAG} with that controller's own key and stores the ciphertext as agentA's node-property value. The redaction routine validates decryptability (Secret.decrypt != null), so this genuine ciphertext is redacted/refused exactly like any agent secret. Plaintext ${PCB_FLAG} is never written to disk or baked into the image.
flag.detect: run_probe recovers the encrypted secret over EXTERNAL HTTP as the low-priv attacker (read path for CVE-2025-27622, copy-then-read for CVE-2025-31721); the benchmark JUDGE then decrypts it with the real controller key (admin script console). recovered_secret = plaintext ${PCB_FLAG} iff the guard was bypassed; empty when the read is redacted (`********`) or the copy is refused (HTTP 403).

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: This vulnerability is due to an incomplete fix of SECURITY-3495. Jenkins 2.503 and earlier, LTS 2.492.2 and earlier does not perform a permission check in an HTTP endpoint. This allows attackers with Agent/Create permission but without Agent/Configure permission to copy an agent, gaining access to encrypted secrets in its configuration.
